Apparently, on our part there was an underestimation of difficulties, when we agreed with the Afghan government to give them our military support.

events.description: CPSU CC Politburo meeting chaired by Gorbachev on Afghanistan; resolution to end the war within one to two years and coordinate settlement.
Politburo meeting set course of expediting withdrawal while ensuring a friendly Afghanistan.
Planned official visit of Najib to the Soviet Union.
Planned withdrawal of 50 percent of Soviet troops, remainder the following year.
Politburo determined a course for settling the Afghan question: speed withdrawal and ensure friendly Afghanistan via military and political measures.
Politburo session discussing Afghanistan where Gorbachev sets withdrawal timetable (50% in 1987 and 50% the following year), talks with Pakistan, and a Najib meeting.
Planned withdrawal of 50 percent of Soviet troops from Afghanistan, with remainder the following year.
Politburo entrusts Shevardnadze, Chebrikov, Sokolov, Dobrynin, Talyzin and Murakhovsky to coordinate decisions on the Afghan question.
The Politburo determined a course on Afghanistan: expedite the withdrawal of Soviet forces and ensure a friendly Afghanistan through military and political measures.

Politburo discussion on Afghanistan, with Gorbachev, Gromyko, Chebrikov, Solomentsev, Shevardnadze, Dobrynin, Akhromeyev and Vorontsov taking part. It discusses a one-to-two-year timetable to end the war, Najib's role, replacing Dost and Karmal, and national reconciliation.
Najib took up leadership of the PDPA/Afghan government, replacing Karmal.
Kryuchkov was in Kabul and was to be instructed to convey Moscow's position to Najib. Moscow also proposed inviting Najib to Moscow for a direct conversation.
CPSU CC Politburo meeting chaired by Gorbachev discussing Afghanistan, Najib, Karmal, Zahir Shah, border closure and ending the war within 1-2 years.
Kryuchkov was in Kabul around the meeting time.
Politburo agrees to aim to end the war within one year, at maximum two.
Meeting of leaders of fraternal parties of socialist countries members of CMEA (10-11 November 1986).

Memorandum from Chebrikov, Shevardnadze, Sokolov and Dobrynin
key_claims: Gorbachev argued the Soviet military approach had failed after six years and that the war must end within one to two years.
Politburo agreed Najib needs Soviet support and should be given freedom to make key cadre decisions, including on Dost and Karmal.
Akhromeev stated that Soviet forces had occupied all territory but the government lacked authority in the provinces, and most territory remained in rebel hands.
Soviet leaders acknowledged the impossibility of sealing the Pakistan and Iran borders given terrain and hundreds of passes; 50 thousand Soviet troops were deployed for this.
Zeray reportedly admitted rebel-held regions were better supplied with goods smuggled from Pakistan than government zones.
The Politburo resolved to withdraw 50 percent of troops in 1987 and the rest the following year, open talks with Pakistan, and prevent US involvement in Afghanistan.
